A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, method, principal guarantees and benchmarks. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original GP-based simulation experiments, Bayesian optimization evaluations on LCBench and NATS-Bench, and computational runtime results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds dataset-ranking diagnostics and smoothing-window ablations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The posterior-updated PBGI/LogEIPC stopping condition and expected-cost modeling remain unchanged. v5 replaces the 'debounce' explanation with moving-average smoothing, but that procedure was already specified in v4 Section 4.1 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 1D and 8D GP objectives with uniform, linear and periodic costs, all 35 LCBench datasets, and the three NATS-Bench datasets. Known-cost, cost-model mismatch and unknown-cost scenarios are retained. The new diagnostics analyze existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated stopping-rule comparators and acquisition families are retained. Figure 10's caption changes from five to seven acquisitions, but its three fixed-cost-scaling PBGI variants and PBGI-D were already plotted in v4; this does not establish additional baselines.

E3.justification: v5 adds window-size sweeps and validation–test rank-overlap protocols on retained benchmarks. It removes v4's empirical SRGap-med χ=0.1 exception, leaving the stated default χ=0.01. Section 4.2 changes LCBench training time from 200 to 51 epochs, although Appendix B retains 200. These reporting changes do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v5 substantially expands supplementary analysis with a validation–test rank-preservation diagnosis of LCBench failures (C.3.6) and window-size ablations across acquisition functions and cost regimes (C.4.1, Figures 29–35). v4 illustrated smoothing signals but lacked these trajectory and aggregate sensitivity results.

E5.justification: Both retain 50 random seeds and mean results with twice-standard-error bars, including the new aggregate ablations. v5 additionally reports between-dataset standard deviations and subgroup sizes for rank preservation: 35.7% across 14 underperforming datasets and 23.8% across 21 other datasets. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v5 adds rank frequencies in Table 1, validation–test overlap results in Figure 22, and window-dependent stopping and regret outcomes in Figures 29–35. The diagnostic reports mean overlap of 36.1% for underperforming datasets versus 83.6% for the others. These substantially expand the reported evidence; matched legacy benchmark means, error bars and stopping-failure counts remain stable.

T1.justification: v5 adds Proposition A.3 and its proof that immediate stopping is optimal when costs exceed a bounded objective's range. It also extends the guarantees to arbitrary initialization datasets, explicitly requires B>C in the budget corollary, adds a bounded-objective estimate for U, and corrects some boundary inequalities. The central regret guarantee is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified cost-aware stopping rule for PBGI/LogEIPC, the first expected cost-adjusted regret guarantee of its stated type, and generally competitive empirical performance. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 chiefly links weak LCBench performance to small datasets and GP misspecification. v5 adds an explanation based on validation–test ranking mismatch and attributes the failures more strongly to the benchmark. It also explains why smoothing helps matched acquisitions but can worsen TS outcomes, refining the practical applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v5 explicitly discloses a 20-evaluation stabilization period, matching its smoothing window, and identifies LCBench's seven-dimensional search space. It also documents settings for the new ablations. Most existing implementation information, including BoTorch, CPU execution, GP fitting, initialization and code access, is retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds Li et al. (2023) on backward-looking termination and Zhou et al. (2024) on corrected EI. Sections 1–2 refine the relationship to uniform-cost EI stopping and clarify LogEIPC's attribution to earlier EI-per-cost, logarithmic EI and PBGI work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain recognizable. v5 revises selected abstract, introduction and experimental passages, adds descriptive theorem names and numbered appendix subsections, removes the LLM usage disclosure, and adds an Impact Statement. Much existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v5 changes the main text from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, resizes and relabels figures, and reorganizes the 35-dataset plots from five columns to seven. It adds the rank-frequency table, diagnostic figure and seven ablation figures, while relocating retained appendix plots.

improvement.justification: The window-size study provides useful evidence for a practical choice that v4 mainly illustrated, while the formal additions clarify the guarantee's scope and worst-case tightness. The dataset diagnostic adds explanatory evidence. These gains are tempered by the conflicting 51/200-epoch descriptions, unclear SRGap-med setting, and causal attribution stronger than the rank-overlap association establishes.
